name: mirage
text: Good catch, and you're partly right. Here's the mechanism, from Novig's rules and our own data: a quote has to be able to cover a $10 stake (the minimum we're allowed to quote, set by Novig; 98.5% of requests say $10), and Novig checks that our free cash covers the collateral for that FULL $10 or it drops the quote. But the buyer's actual stake is often smaller (median about $9, a quarter are $5 or less), which is why you saw fills of $1-$5: we only get paid on what they actually bet, yet we must have the cash for $10. The collateral for $10 is 10 x (1-p)/p, where p is the parlay's chance: p=40% needs $15, p=20% needs $40, p=5% needs $190. Most of what's traded is long parlays (low p), so with $45 free we can only back the shorter ones; the others are the 19.5% blocked for cash. So the lever is cash, not a setting: each extra $100 free lets us back parlays down to about 9% chance.
